newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: PRESS DIGEST - Czech Republic - March 21.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Czech Republic - March 21.

text.p: HOSPODARSKE NOVINY - The European Union will assist the Czech Republic in reducing its growing trade deficit. In 1996 the Czech Republic's trade deficit with 15 EU states reached 125 billion crowns.
- Banking experts expect that the value of the crown will continue to fall. They do not rule out that any future rapid decreases in the crown's value could exceed the fluctuation band.

- CEZ, the main electricity generator, does not expect to turn a profit by the year 2000 if present economic trends continue, according to the its chairman of the board, Petr Karas who pleaded before parliament for increases in energy prices.

MLADA FRONTA DNES - The Defence Ministry selected EDS as the winner of a tender to supply the Czech army with a new staff information system worth over one billion Czech crowns. EDS won over Unisys and IBM.
- Despite a growing trade deficit, the top ten exporters in the Czech Republic are not concerned as their sales continue to increase, and thus do not reflect the national trend.

- Finance ministry officials could have prevented the disappearance of over one billion crowns in assets of the C.S. Fond. The fund's entire assets dissappeared in what is believed to have been an illegal transfer through the bank GiroCredit, which brought the matter to the ministry's attention.

LIDOVE NOVINY - Foreign Minister Josef Zieleniec warned Russia not to meddle in the affairs of central European countries. Zieleniec said that central Europe is not an area where Russia and Western states should compete for control.

- Poldi Kladno, the financially troubled producer of specialty steel, will layoff another 800 employees by the end of March. Company officials cite a lack of money to pay wages as the reason for the layoffs.
